albums.blurb: Takada is a Tokyo percussionist who trained in Western classical performance, played with the RIAS Symphony Orchestra in Berlin, and then turned away from the orchestral world to study African and Asian percussion traditions. Through the Looking Glass, her first solo record, was cut for RCA Japan in 1983 with Takada playing everything herself — marimba, gong, ocarina, reed organ, vibraphone, even Coca-Cola bottles — across a four-piece suite that is entirely instrumental. The album sank without trace on release, resurfaced decades later as a collector's grail passed around online, and was finally reissued in 2017 by Palto Flats and WRWTFWW Records.
albums.reception: Pitchfork's review of the 2017 reissue called it "one of the most dazzling works of minimalism, be it from the East or West," and the reissue became the second-best-selling album on Discogs that year.

albums.blurb: Lenae is a Chicago singer who emerged in the mid-2010s from the Zero Fatigue collective alongside Smino and producer Monte Booker, releasing a string of EPs before her 2022 debut album Hypnos. Bird's Eye, her second full-length for Atlantic, is a compact eleven-track, thirty-five-minute set featuring guest appearances from Childish Gambino on "One Wish" and Ty Dolla $ign on "Dream Girl." It sharpened her airy, high-register soul writing into some of the most direct songs of her catalog.
albums.reception: Its lead single "Love Me Not" became a delayed breakout after going viral in late 2024, giving Lenae her first-ever Billboard Hot 100 entry and eventually climbing to No. 5 on the chart in 2025.

albums.blurb: Clube da Esquina — "the corner club" — was a loose collective of musicians from Minas Gerais gathered around Milton Nascimento, then in his late twenties, and Lô Borges, a 19-year-old guitarist whose family home hosted the group. Their 1972 double album for EMI-Odeon fuses Minas folk melodies, jazz harmony, and Beatles-scale studio pop, with orchestrations by Eumir Deodato and Wagner Tiso conducted by Paulo Moura, and it launched the careers of collaborators like Beto Guedes and Toninho Horta. It stands at the center of post-bossa Brazilian music, a regional answer to both tropicália and Anglo-American psychedelia.
albums.reception: Rolling Stone Brasil ranked it the seventh greatest Brazilian album of all time, and in 2022 the Discoteca Básica podcast's critics' poll of the 500 greatest Brazilian records placed it at No. 1.
